one_liner: An overnight polysomnogram revealed moderate obstructive sleep apnea syndrome and moderate periodic limb movement in sleep disorder, and the patient is recommended for CPAP titration, ENT evaluation, and behavioral weight loss.

problems.name: Periodic limb movement in sleep disorder

key_findings.name: Minimum oxygen saturation
key_findings.interpretation: Minimum oxygen saturation dropped to 88% during overnight polysomnogram.

key_findings.name: Apnea-hypopnea index
key_findings.interpretation: Overall apnea-hypopnea index of 15.2 events per hour in the supine position.

key_findings.name: Periodic limb movements index
key_findings.interpretation: Overall index of 32 events per hour of sleep.

procedures.name: Overnight polysomnogram
procedures.outcome: Demonstrated moderate obstructive sleep apnea and periodic limb movement in sleep disorder with reduced sleep efficiency.

course.narrative: The patient underwent an overnight polysomnogram which showed moderate obstructive sleep apnea syndrome with an AHI of 15.2 events per hour in the supine position, minimum oxygen saturation of 88%, and moderate periodic limb movement in sleep disorder with an index of 32 events per hour. Sleep efficiency was reduced to 89.2% with significant sleep fragmentation and diminished REM sleep. The patient is advised to return for a repeat overnight polysomnogram with CPAP titration, undergo an ENT/maxillofacial evaluation, avoid evening sedatives and alcohol, and participate in a behavioral weight loss program.

action_items.action: Return to the sleep laboratory for repeat overnight polysomnogram with CPAP titration.
action_items.rationale: To determine a necessary pressure to prevent apneas and treat obstructive sleep apnea.

action_items.action: Undergo careful ENT/maxillofacial evaluation by a physician familiar with sleep disorders.
action_items.rationale: Anatomical abnormalities in the upper airway often cause or predispose to this condition.

action_items.action: Participate in a behavioral weight loss program.
action_items.rationale: Obstructive sleep apnea is worsened by obesity.

red_flags.message: Obstructive sleep apnea is associated with increased risk of myocardial infarction, stroke and sudden death, and excessive daytime sleepiness while driving.
